title: Your Wi-Fi uses the same frequency as your microwave #Shorts

yt.title: Your Wi-Fi uses the same frequency as your microwave #Shorts
yt.description:
Microwave ovens run at about 2.45 GHz, inside the 2.4 GHz band Wi-Fi also uses. Wavelength = c / f.
Narration is AI-generated.

scenes.text: Your Wi-Fi uses the same frequency as your microwave
scenes.narration: Your Wi-Fi uses the same frequency as your microwave.

scenes.label: Wi-Fi band and microwave ovens
scenes.narration: Both run near two point four gigahertz.
The wavelength is the speed of light divided by the frequency. That's about {c_cm_say} centimeters per wave.

scenes.text: Door holes: a few mm. Waves: {c_cm} cm.
scenes.narration: The holes in the door are tiny next to that, so the waves can't get out.
And your router is thousands of times weaker. It just carries data.
Ever noticed your Wi-Fi drop when the microwave runs?
